title: Oaylleeaght
description: Ten short stories about science and technology: pictures from a rover on Mars, a lemon battery in a physics class, a gymnast in a sports science room, a spelling programme for Manx, a photographer of spider webs, a letter from a scientist following elephants in Kenya, old crafts and machines in a folk museum, a tidal causeway to an islet, new machines and a strike at a factory, and a school meeting about phones.

lessons.title: Jallooyn veih'n rouailtagh
lessons.summary: Cressida Holloway, a science teacher in Douglas, shows sixteen-year-old Tarquin Ellwood pictures from the rover on Mars: signals from the distant planet take minutes of sixty seconds to arrive, the rocks lie in layers, and scientists have a hypothesis that water made them, so the rover looks for the presence of water and of life; in one picture a small blue dot is the Earth, and Cressida explains periodic comets and the jets of the rocket.
lessons.text:
Ta Cressida Holloway ny ynseyder oaylleeaght ayns ard-scoill ayns Doolish. Dagh Jeheiney, tra ta'n scoill harrish, t'ee jeeaghyn jallooyn noa veih Mart da possan beg dy scollagyn. Jiu, cha nel agh un scollag ayn: Tarquin Ellwood, shey bleeaney jeig d'eash.

“Cre ta shen?” dooyrt Tarquin, as eh jeeaghyn er y jalloo mooar er y voalley.

“She jalloo veih'n rouailtagh eh,” dooyrt Cressida. “She gleashtan beg eh, gyn dooinney erbee ayn, as t'eh goll mygeayrt er Mart. Ta'n rouailtagh goaill jallooyn as cur ad dys y Chruinney.”

“Vel ny jallooyn çheet dy tappee?”

“Cha nel. Ta Mart feer fadaneagh. Ta'n cowrey veih'n rouailtagh goaill kuse dy minnidyn dy roshtyn ain. Ta tree feed tullagh ayns dagh minnid, as ta'n cowrey goll trooid dagh tullagh jeu foddey, foddey. Ta Mart foddey ny smoo fadaneagh na'n eayst.”

Ayns y jalloo noa, va creg ard. Va'n chreg jeant jeh straneyn, strane er strane, myr duillagyn ayns lioar.

“Ta sheinys ec ny oaylleeyn mychione ny straneyn shoh,” dooyrt Cressida. “Rere y sheinys, va ushtey er Mart keayrt dy row, as ren yn ushtey shen ny straneyn. Ta'n rouailtagh shirrey faare ushtey 'sy chreg nish. My vees faare ushtey ayn, foddee dy row bea ayn neesht. Cha nel fys ec peiagh erbee er beays bea er Mart foast. Agh my hig y rouailtagh er beays bea veg, bee shen naight vooar.”

Ayns jalloo elley, va ponk beg gorrym 'syn aer.

“She rollage yn ponk shen?” dooyrt Tarquin.

“Cha nee,” dooyrt Cressida. “She'n Chruinney ain hene eh. Ta shin ooilley cummal er y ponk beg shen.”

Lurg shen, ren Tarquin feysht mychione comaidyn. Dooyrt Cressida dy vel comaidyn earishagh ayn: comaid earishagh, t'ee çheet erash dys y ghrian reesht as reesht, lurg ny smoo na keead blein ny keayrtyn. Honnick yn ayr echey comaid earishagh tra v'eh aeg, dooyrt Tarquin.

Ec y jerrey, hoilshee Cressida feeshan da. Va'n lhong-spoar goll seose veih'n Chruinney, lesh skioot mooar dy aile as dy jaagh fo. Tra haink y rouailtagh sheese er Mart, va skiootyn beggey er y lhong, as haink ee sheese dy meein as dy sauçhey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n rouailtagh?
She gleashtan beg eh, gyn dooinney erbee ayn, as t'eh goll mygeayrt er Mart.
Vel tree feed tullagh ayns dagh minnid?
Ta. Ta tree feed tullagh ayns dagh minnid.
Cre'n sheinys ta ec ny oaylleeyn mychione ny straneyn?
Rere y sheinys, va ushtey er Mart keayrt dy row, as ren yn ushtey ny straneyn.
Cre'n ponk beg gorrym va 'sy jalloo?
She'n Chruinney eh.
Cre ta'n rouailtagh shirrey 'sy chreg?
T'eh shirrey faare ushtey, son dy vel faare ushtey cowrey er beays bea.
Cre honnick Tarquin 'sy feeshan?
Honnick eh yn lhong-spoar goll seose, lesh skioot mooar dy aile as dy jaagh fo.

lessons.title: Lectraghys ass limon
lessons.summary: Osric Fairlie, a physics teacher in Ramsey, has the room prepared for an experiment: after a word on safety, about mercury in old thermometers and lead, his pupils weigh a kilogram of lemons, link them with cables and light a small lamp; Hermione Bradshaw compares a lemon with a potato and pours the juice into a glass, and the potato does better.
lessons.text:
Ta Osric Fairlie ny ynseyder fishag ayns ard-scoill ayns Rhumsaa. S'mie lesh e scollagyn y fishag, son dy vel eh jannoo prowaltys dagh shiaghtin. Jiu, va'n shamyr aarlit echey roish my haink ny scollagyn stiagh: va limonyn, caabylyn, peeshyn beggey dy veain as sollys beg er dagh boayrd.

“Roish my nee shin toshiaght,” dooyrt Osric, “ta shin loayrt mychione sauçhys. Ta sauçhys ny share na prowaltys erbee. Ta caabylyn as ushtey limon ayns y phrowaltys, as cha nel ushtey limon mie son ny sooillyn. Myr shen, ta glonney son ny sooillyn er dagh boayrd. Shoh sauçhys.”

Hoilshee eh shenn ghlonney da ny scollagyn, lesh red gial ayn. “She mercur shoh,” dooyrt eh. “Ayns ny laghyn shenn, va mercur ayns dagh glonney son towse çhiass. Agh ta mercur nieu, as cha nel shin jannoo ymmyd jeh 'sy scoill nish. Ta leoaie nieu neesht. Va leoaie ayns peint keayrt dy row. Cha nel mercur ny leoaie ayns y phrowaltys jiu.”

Ec y chied boayrd, va Hermione Bradshaw. Ren ish as e caarjyn trimmid ny limonyn y howse. Va kilogram dy limonyn oc, as va jeih limonyn ayns y kilogram shen.

“Cur daa pheesh dy veain ayns dagh limon,” dooyrt Osric. “Nish, s'egin diu ny limonyn y chiangley ry-cheilley lesh ny caabylyn, as y caabyl s'jerree y chiangley rish y sollys beg.”

Ren ad shen. Va'n sollys beg er, agh cha row eh feer gial.

“Ta lectraghys çheet ass ny limonyn!” dooyrt Hermione.

“Ta,” dooyrt Osric. “Nish, ta mee laccal oo dy chormal limon rish praase. Cre'n fer ta jannoo ny smoo dy lectraghys?”

Ghow Hermione praase as limon. Hug ee meain ayns y phraase, as hug ee y caabyl eddyr y praase as y sollys beg. V'ee cormal y daa red rish tammylt. Va'n sollys ny s'gilley lesh y phraase.

Lurg shen, ren ee limon y ghiarey, as ren ee deayrt yn ushtey ass y limon stiagh ayns glonney. Ren Osric deayrt yn ushtey ass praase brisht stiagh ayns glonney elley.

“Shoh yn ushtey ta jannoo y lectraghys,” dooyrt Osric. “Cha nel yn ushtey 'sy phraase cha geyre as yn ushtey 'sy limon, agh t'eh jannoo ny smoo dy lectraghys. Cha row fys aym er shen tra va mee aeg.”

Va ny scollagyn ooilley cormal ny towshanyn oc. Va'n phrowaltys aarlit dy mie, as cha row doilleeid erbee ayn son sauçhys. “Shen y fishag,” dooyrt Osric. “Ta'n fishag ayns dagh red, eer ayns limon.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre va aarlit ec Osric roish my haink ny scollagyn?
Va limonyn, caabylyn, peeshyn meain as sollys beg er dagh boayrd.
Cre'n fa nagh vel mercur 'sy scoill nish?
Son dy vel mercur nieu.
Vel kilogram dy limonyn trome?
Cha nel. Va jeih limonyn ayns y kilogram.
Cre ren Hermione deayrt stiagh ayns y glonney?
Ren ee deayrt yn ushtey ass y limon stiagh ayns y glonney.
Cre'n fer va jannoo ny smoo dy lectraghys?
Va'n praase jannoo ny smoo dy lectraghys na'n limon.

lessons.title: Yn lheiltagh as y fer fyshoaylleeaght
lessons.summary: Delilah Pembroke, a nineteen-year-old gymnast from Peel, has pain in her shoulder and goes to the sports science room in Douglas, where Lysander Thwaite, an expert in physiology, works with hurling players, riders and runners; a blood test shows muscle enzymes after hard training, and he tells her that she does not need an operation, only rest and exercises.
lessons.text:
Ta Delilah Pembroke ny lheiltagh. T'ee nuy bleeaney jeig d'eash, as t'ee cummal ayns Purt ny h-Inshey. Ta Delilah traenal ayns Doolish shey laaghyn dagh shiaghtin, as t'ee lheim, çhyndaa as croghey er ny laueyn eck. Agh rish mee nish, ta pian ayns y gheaylin eck. Ta'n pian ny smoo tra t'ee croghey er ny laueyn.

Hie Delilah dys y thie oaylleeaght spoyrt ayns Doolish. Ta Lysander Thwaite gobbraghey ayn. Ta Lysander ny oayllee fyshoaylleeaght. She oaylleeaght y chorp eh y fyshoaylleeaght: kys ta'n cree, y fuill as ny craueyn gobbraghey.

Ta Lysander gobbraghey marish sleih veih ymmodee spoyrtyn. Ta cloieder immanaght ayn veih Nerin: she shenn spoyrt ass Nerin ee immanaght, gollrish y chammag ain. Ta ben aeg ayn ta jannoo markiaght: t'ee lheim harrish boallaghyn er cabbyl mooar. As ta dooinney ayn ta roie dagh moghrey, as ta Lysander towse y cree echey.

“Shoh yn obbyr aym,” dooyrt Lysander. “Ta fyshoaylleeaght y lheiltagh anchasley rish fyshoaylleeaght cloieder immanaght, ny jeh ben ta jannoo markiaght. Agh ta pian ayns y gheaylin cadjin ayns ymmodee spoyrtyn.”

Ghow eh beggan fuill veih Delilah. Ayns y fuill, va ensyme jeh'n eill. Dooyrt Lysander dy vel yn ensyme shoh çheet stiagh 'sy fuill tra ta'n eill brisht beggan lurg traenal trome.

“Vel feme aym er obbreeaght?” dooyrt Delilah. Va aggle urree. Va obbreeaght er y gheaylin ec lheiltagh elley 'sy phossan eck, as cha daink ee erash dys y spoyrt.

“Cha nel,” dooyrt Lysander. “Cha nel feme ayd er obbreeaght. Cha nel y geaylin brisht. Ta'n ensyme ayns dty uill son dy row oo traenal ro trome. S'egin dhyt lhiggey da'n gheaylin rish kiare shiaghtinyn, as jannoo ny cliaghtaghyn aym dagh laa.”

Ren Delilah myr dooyrt eh. Lurg kiare shiaghtinyn, va'n pian ersooyl, as v'ee croghey er ny laueyn reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta fyshoaylleeaght?
She oaylleeaght y chorp ee: kys ta'n cree, y fuill as ny craueyn gobbraghey.
Quoi ta gobbraghey marish Lysander?
Ta cloieder immanaght, ben ta jannoo markiaght as dooinney ta roie.
Cre va ayns fuill Delilah?
Va ensyme jeh'n eill ayns y fuill eck.
Row feme ec Delilah er obbreeaght?
Cha row. Cha row agh feme eck er kiare shiaghtinyn gyn traenal, as er cliaghtaghyn.

lessons.title: Claare lettraghey son y Ghaelg
lessons.summary: Leonora Faulkner, a programmer in Douglas, is the maker of a spelling programme for Manx: she explains to the teacher Horatio Blyth her principle that the programme learns from texts, the trouble with eclipsis, the dative and the imperative, and how Arabic, written as an abjad of consonants, is harder still for computers; in a test it misses only one misspelt word in ten, and the programme will be out shortly.
lessons.text:
Ta Leonora Faulkner gobbraghey lesh co-earrooderyn ayns Doolish. She jeantagh claareyn ee. Nish, t'ee jannoo claare lettraghey son y Ghaelg. My ta fockle screeuit dy olk, nee yn claare cowrey jiarg y chur fo.

Haink Horatio Blyth, ynseyder Gaelg, dys yn oik eck. V'eh laccal toiggal kys ta'n claare gobbraghey.

“Ta un phrinsabyl aym,” dooyrt Leonora. “Cha nel mee ginsh da'n claare ny reillyn ooilley. Ta'n claare lhaih ymmodee screeuyn, as t'eh ynsaghey veih ny screeuyn. Shen y prinsabyl. Agh ta'n Ghaelg doillee son claare.”

“Cre'n fa?” dooyrt Horatio.

“Smooinee er stronnaghys,” dooyrt ee. “Lurg 'nyn', ta 'thie' caghlaa gys 'dhie': 'nyn dhie'. Ta'n stronnaghys caghlaa toshiaght y fockle. Ta'n claare fakin fockle noa, as cha nel fys echey dy nee'n fockle shenn eh. Smooinee er y toyrtagh neesht. Ayns ny shenn screeuyn, ta'n toyrtagh caghlaa jerrey y fockle ny keayrtyn. As ta'n mod oardreilagh ayn: 'jean', 'tar', 'immee'. Ta ny focklyn oardreilagh giare as anchasley rish ny focklyn elley.”

Hoilshee ee lioar Arabish da. “Ta'n Arabish ny s'doillee foast,” dooyrt ee. “She abjad eh. Ayns abjad, ta ny corocklyn screeuit, agh cha nel ny lettyryn elley screeuit dy cadjin. S'egin da'n lhaihder smooinaghtyn er y fockle slane. Ta abjad mie son sleih, agh t'eh doillee son co-earrooder.”

Smooinee Horatio rish tammylt. “Myr shen, ta'n Ghaelg ny sloo doillee na'n Arabish?”

“Ta,” dooyrt Leonora. “Agh foast cha nel y claare kiart dagh keayrt. Ghow mee lioar giare as hug mee eh da'n claare. Va'n corrillagh mie dy liooar: va un fockle screeuit dy olk ayns jeih nagh dooar y claare. Ta'n corrillagh shen ny share na v'eh 'sy vee roish shoh, tra va un fockle ayns queig caillit.”

“Cre'n traa vees y claare ry-gheddyn?” dooyrt Horatio.

“Dy gerrid,” dooyrt y jeantagh. “Dy gerrid, foddee dagh scollag 'sy Vunscoill y chlaare y ghoaill er y cho-earrooder ec y thie. As gerrid ny yei shen, bee eh ry-gheddyn er yn eddyr-voggyl son dagh peiagh.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Leonora jannoo?
She jeantagh claareyn ee, as t'ee jannoo claare lettraghey son y Ghaelg.
Cre'n prinsabyl t'ec Leonora?
Ta'n claare lhaih ymmodee screeuyn as ynsaghey veih ny screeuyn.
Cre ta abjad?
Ayns abjad, ta ny corocklyn screeuit, agh cha nel ny lettyryn elley screeuit dy cadjin.
Cre'n fa ta stronnaghys doillee son y claare?
Son dy vel y stronnaghys caghlaa toshiaght y fockle.
Cre ta'n toyrtagh as y mod oardreilagh jannoo?
Ta'n toyrtagh caghlaa jerrey y fockle ny keayrtyn, as ta ny focklyn oardreilagh giare as anchasley.
Cre va'n corrillagh?
Va un fockle screeuit dy olk ayns jeih nagh dooar y claare.
Cre'n traa vees y claare ry-gheddyn?
Dy gerrid.

lessons.title: Eggaghyn feeit er y drine
lessons.summary: Cyrus Wetherby, a retired man near Sulby who loves photography, has watched a television series on insects and, early one autumn morning, photographs the woven webs of spiders on the lower branches of the blackthorn in his garden, among the sloes; near the bush, plants that spread by rhizomes give the spiders shelter, and his extensive collection of pictures goes to a local magazine.
lessons.text:
Ta Cyrus Wetherby cummal ayns thie beg faggys da Sulby. T'eh ersooyl veih'n obbyr nish, as t'eh cur y traa echey da fotografeeaght. Ta fotografeeaght ny red feer vie da: t'eh goaill jallooyn jeh ushagyn, blaaghyn as beishteigyn.

'Sy tourey, honnick Cyrus straih noa er y çhellveeish mychione beishteigyn. Va shey episodeyn ayns y straih. Ayns ny episodeyn shen, va oayllee ginsh mychione y sniengan. Ta'n sniengan jannoo eggey feeit ass stoo ta çheet ass e chorp hene, as t'eh goaill beishteigyn beggey 'syn eggey shen. Ayns un jeh ny episodeyn, va jallooyn feer vie jeh eggaghyn feeit lesh ushtey er.

Ayns y garey echey, ta drine mooar. She drine airn eh. 'Sy fouyir, ta airnyn gorrym-doo er y drine. Ta'n airn geyre as soor, agh ta sleih jannoo jough jeh. Un moghrey 'sy fouyir, hie Cyrus magh roish y ghrian. Va eggaghyn feeit er y drine ooilley: ram jeu. Va ny smoo er ny crouwyn eeghtyragh na er ny crouwyn ard. Va'n sniengan cummal ec y fraue jeh'n drine, as va ny beishteigyn getlagh faggys da'n thalloo, myr shen va ny crouwyn eeghtyragh share son yn eggey.

Ghow Cyrus ram jallooyn jeh ny eggaghyn as jeh ny airnyn. Ren eh y dorrys y aagail foslit, as haink e ven magh. Va lioar foslit eck mychione lossreeyn.

“Jeeagh er ny lossreeyn shoh fo'n drine,” dooyrt ee. “T'ad gaase veih raisoamyn. Ta ny raisoamyn goll fo'n thalloo, as ta lossreeyn noa gaase seose veih ny raisoamyn. Ta'n sniengan cummal mastey ny lossreeyn shen neesht.”

Ec y jerrey, va çhaglym rheamyssagh dy jallooyn ec Cyrus: ny smoo na keead jalloo. Hug eh y çhaglym rheamyssagh shen da earishlioar 'sy valley. Ayns y nah earishlioar, va jalloo jeh eggey feeit er y drine er y chied duillag.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Cyrus jannoo lesh y traa echey?
T'eh cur y traa echey da fotografeeaght.
Cre honnick Cyrus er y çhellveeish?
Honnick eh straih lesh shey episodeyn mychione beishteigyn.
C'raad va ny smoo eggaghyn?
Va ny smoo eggaghyn er ny crouwyn eeghtyragh.
Cre va foslit ec ben Cyrus?
Va lioar foslit eck mychione lossreeyn.
Kys ta ny lossreeyn fo'n drine gaase?
T'ad gaase veih raisoamyn fo'n thalloo.
Cre hug Cyrus da'n earishlioar?
Hug eh çhaglym rheamyssagh dy jallooyn da'n earishlioar.

lessons.title: Lettyr veih ny elefantyn
lessons.summary: In a letter to her brother Ferdinand in Castletown, the Manx scientist Araminta Colebrook writes from a mountainous park in Kenya, where she lives in a hut and follows elephants with small devices on their necks: the elephants cross the boundary of the park and do damage on the farms, refugees from a war work with her, the diversity of life is great, she has had a fever, and she has sent an appeal to the government for a fence.
lessons.text:
Ferdinand veen,

Ta mee screeu hood veih Kenya. Ta mee er ve ayns shoh three meeghyn nish, as ta mee gobbraghey lesh ny elefantyn. Ta'n boayl sleitoil: ta sleityn ard mygeayrt mooin, as ta'n raad seose dys y bwaane aym foddey as doillee. She bwaane beg eh, lesh un shamyr, agh ta lectraghys ayn veih'n ghrian, as ta'n co-earrooder aym gobbraghey ayn.

Ta mee er chur red beg lectragh er mwannal shiaght elefantyn. Ta dagh red beg cur cowrey dys my cho-earrooder dagh oor, as ta fys aym c'raad ta dagh elefant. Ta jeoraght er y phairk, agh cha nel fys ec ny elefantyn er y jeoraght shen. Ny keayrtyn, t'ad goll harrish y jeoraght as stiagh er y gowaltys ta faggys da'n phairk. Ta'n gowaltys shen ec eirinagh as e lught-thie. Ta'n elefant mooar as trome, as t'eh jannoo jeeill vooar er y gowaltys: t'eh brishey ny cleighyn as gee ny lossreeyn. Va jeeill er three gowaltys 'sy vee shoh.

Ta kuse dy kemmyrkee gobbraghey marym. Haink ad veih çheer elley, raad ta caggey. Va kemmyrkagh aeg, Deng yn ennym echey, ny ynseyder ayns y çheer echey roish y chaggey. Nish t'eh coontey ny elefantyn marym, as t'eh gynsaghey Baarle da paitçhyn ny kemmyrkee 'sy champ.

Ta'n neuchaslid dy vea ayns shoh yindyssagh. Er yn un laa, honnick mee elefantyn, ushagyn jiarg as gorrym, as beishteigyn nagh vaik mee rieau roie. Ta'n neuchaslid shoh mooar ny smoo na neuchaslid Ellan Vannin, ga dy vel yn ellan ain aalin.

Va çhiassagh orrym 'sy vee shoh. Rish tree laa, cha dod mee goll magh ass y bwaane. Ta çhiassagh cadjin ayns ny buill sleitoil shoh. Agh ta'n çhiassagh ersooyl nish, as ta mee mie.

Ec y jerrey, hug mee aghin da'n reiltys. Ta mee laccal argid son cleigh lectragh mygeayrt y phairk. Lesh y cleigh shen, cha jig ny elefantyn er gowaltys erbee, as bee ny eirinee sauçhey. Ta mee jerkal dy jean y reiltys clashtyn rish yn aghin aym.

Slane lhiat, as cur my ghraih da ny paitçhyn ayns Balley Chashtal.

Araminta

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta Araminta cummal?
T'ee cummal ayns bwaane beg ayns boayl sleitoil ayns Kenya.
Cre ta ny elefantyn jannoo er y gowaltys?
T'ad jannoo jeeill: t'ad brishey ny cleighyn as gee ny lossreeyn.
Quoi ta gobbraghey marish Araminta?
Ta kuse dy kemmyrkee gobbraghey marish.
Cre'n aghin hug ee da'n reiltys?
Hug ee aghin son argid son cleigh lectragh mygeayrt y phairk.
Row çhiassagh er Araminta?
Va. Va çhiassagh urree rish tree laa.

lessons.title: Shenn obbyr laue 'sy thie tashtee
lessons.summary: Fourteen-year-old Dulcie Haworth visits a folk museum with her grandfather Ebenezer: they see a potter's wheel and pottery, shoes of leather, linen woven by hand and cotton from mechanical looms, and an old mechanical piano; Ebenezer shares a memory of his grandmother weaving linen, and tells Dulcie that he is the heir of her old wheel, which Dulcie will have one day.
lessons.text:
Ta Dulcie Haworth kiare bleeaney jeig d'eash. Jesarn, hie ee marish y shennayr eck, Ebenezer, dys y thie tashtee feallagh ayns y jiass jeh'n ellan. Ta'n thie tashtee shoh ginsh mychione bea feallagh Vannin roish keead blein: kys va'n feallagh gobbraghey, as kys v'ad jannoo nyn eaddagh.

'Sy chied shamyr, va pasheydys. Va queeyl veg ayn, as va dooinney soie ec y queeyl as jannoo cappan ass cray. “She pasheydys shoh,” dooyrt Ebenezer. “Va pasheydys jeant ayns dagh balley ayns ny laghyn shen, son va cappanyn feme ec dagh lught-thie.”

'Sy nah shamyr, va braagyn jeant ass liare. Va'n liare doo as creoi, agh dooyrt y dooinney 'sy thie tashtee dy row braag liare mie son jeih bleeaney. Va'n liare jeant ass crackan ny baagh.

Ec y jerrey, haink ad gys shamyr lesh eaddagh. Va lieen ayn, feeit lesh y laue, as cadee, jeant ayns thieyn-obbree mooarey ayns Sostyn. “Va'n lieen jeant ayns shoh, ayns Ellan Vannin,” dooyrt Ebenezer. “Agh va'n cadee çheet veih foddey ersooyl. Ayns Sostyn, va greieyn obbrinagh ayns ny thieyn-obbree: va ny greieyn shen jannoo cadee ny s'tappee na thousane ben. Lurg shen, va'n cadee ny sloo deyr na'n lieen.”

Va pianney shenn faggys da'n dorrys. Cha row peiagh erbee cloie er, agh va'n pianney cloie arrane er hene. “She pianney obbrinagh eh,” dooyrt Ebenezer. “Ta pabyr lesh tuill ayn, as ta'n pabyr ginsh da'n pianney cre ny sheeanyn dy chloie.”

Cha dooyrt Ebenezer veg rish tammylt. “Ta cooinaght aym,” dooyrt eh. “Va my shenn-voir jannoo snaie lieen er queeyl veg ayns y thie eck. Ta'n cooinaght shen feer gial foast. V'ee goaill arrane tra v'ee gobbraghey.”

“C'raad ta'n queeyl shen nish?” dooyrt Dulcie.

“T'ee aym,” dooyrt Ebenezer. “Va mish yn eirey eck. Hooar mee yn queeyl as y thie eck. As nish, she uss yn eirey aym. Un laa, bee'n queeyl ayd.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta'n thie tashtee ginsh mychione?
T'eh ginsh mychione bea feallagh Vannin roish keead blein.
Cre va jeant ass liare?
Va braagyn jeant ass liare.
C'raad va'n cadee jeant?
Va'n cadee jeant ayns thieyn-obbree mooarey ayns Sostyn.
Cre'n cooinaght t'ec Ebenezer?
Va'n shenn-voir echey jannoo snaie lieen er queeyl veg.
Cre'n sorçh dy phianney va faggys da'n dorrys?
She pianney obbrinagh eh, as t'eh cloie er hene.
Quoi yn eirey ec Ebenezer?
She Dulcie yn eirey echey.

lessons.title: Yn taagher as yn ellaneen
lessons.summary: Marcella Dunstan, who measures the tides, takes her ten-year-old son Jolyon by bus to an islet that is reachable only at low tide along a stone causeway; at the stop sign she checks the tide times, they climb to a cairn where monks once prayed, meet a tailless Manx cat at the old chapel, see workers with building materials mending the causeway, and come back before the water returns while the weather stays favourable.
lessons.text:
Ta Marcella Dunstan gobbraghey son y reiltys. T'ee towse y tidey ec y traie, as t'ee screeu ny towshanyn ayns co-earrooder. Jesarn, ghow ee y mac eck, Jolyon, jeih bleeaney d'eash, dys ellaneen beg 'sy jiass.

Hie ad lesh y bus. Ec y stap bus, va cassan sheese dys y traie. Va'n ellaneen er y çheu elley jeh'n ushtey, as va taagher eddyr y traie as yn ellaneen: raad jeh claghyn mooarey, goll trooid y vooir.

“Cha nel yn ellaneen roshtynagh agh tra ta'n tidey injil,” dooyrt Marcella. “Tra ta'n tidey ard, ta'n taagher fo'n ushtey. Ta'n ellaneen roshtynagh rish tree ooryn ny jees, as ny lurg shen, cha nel.”

Ec y taagher, va cowrey mooar: “Stap! Jeeagh er y traa.” Ren Marcella stappal, as ren ee jeeaghyn er ny ooryn tidey er y cowrey. “Ta'n tidey injil nish,” dooyrt ee. “As ta'n emshir foayroil: cha nel geay ny fliaghey ayn. Lhig dooin goll.”

Hie ad harrish y taagher. Er yn ellaneen, va cronk beg, as er y mullagh, va carn: possan mooar dy claghyn, er nyn gur ry-cheilley.

“Quoi ren y carn?” dooyrt Jolyon.

“Va maynee cummal ayns shoh, roish thousane blein,” dooyrt Marcella. “Va'n carn ny chowrey son ny maynee. V'ad guee ec y carn dagh moghrey, as v'ad guee 'sy cheeill veg neesht.”

Faggys da'n cheeill veg, va kayt doo. Cha row arbyl erbee echey. “She kayt cuttagh eh!” dooyrt Jolyon. “She kayt cuttagh, kayt Vannin, gyn arbyl,” dooyrt Marcella. Va'n kayt cuttagh cummal ec y fer ta jeeaghyn lurg yn ellaneen.

Er y çheu elley jeh'n ellaneen, va deiney gobbraghey er y taagher. Va stoo troggee oc: claghyn noa, cray as gleashtan beg. “Ta'n tidey jannoo jeeill da'n taagher dagh blein,” dooyrt fer jeu. “Ta shin cur y stoo troggee shoh ayn dy chummal y raad lajer.”

Lurg daa oor, dooyrt Marcella: “Ta'n tidey çheet erash.” Haink ad erash harrish y taagher, as va'n emshir foayroil foast. Tra v'ad ec y stap bus, va'n ushtey harrish y taagher reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n traa ta'n ellaneen roshtynagh?
Ta'n ellaneen roshtynagh tra ta'n tidey injil.
Cre va scruit er y cowrey ec y taagher?
Va “Stap! Jeeagh er y traa” scruit er.
Cre va er mullagh y chronk?
Va carn er y mullagh, raad va maynee guee.
Row'n emshir foayroil?
Va. Cha row geay ny fliaghey ayn, as va'n emshir foayroil.
Cre va ec ny deiney er y taagher?
Va stoo troggee oc: claghyn noa, cray as gleashtan beg.

lessons.title: Ny greieyn noa as y stholk
lessons.summary: A factory in the south of the island buys new machines that work on their own, and the workers fear that eighty jobs will be lost; Clarence Whitmore, who holds the presidency of the workers' society, leads a strike and a protest, the attorney Honora Brackley speaks for the workers, a government officer helps them meet the directors, and they agree that the workers will train for new qualifications to run and mend the machines, so their employment is safe.
lessons.text:
Ta thie-obbree mooar ayns y jiass jeh'n ellan. Ta shey feed obbree gobbraghey ayn, jannoo peeshyn beggey son lhongyn-aer. 'Sy tourey, chionnee ny stiureyderyn greieyn noa. Ta ny greieyn noa gobbraghey nyn lomarcan, gyn peiagh erbee. Va aggle er ny obbreeyn: dooyrt ny stiureyderyn dy beagh kiare feed staartey caillit.

Ta Clarence Whitmore gobbraghey 'sy thie-obbree rish feed blein. T'eh ny eaghtyrane er sheshaght ny obbreeyn neesht. Hooar eh yn eaghtyraneys 'sy vlein shoh, as cha row eh jerkal rieau dy beagh yn eaghtyraneys cha doillee.

“Ta failley mie ain ayns shoh,” dooyrt Clarence rish ny obbreeyn. “Ta'n failley shoh cur argid da shey feed lught-thie. Cha nel mee laccal dy jean shin coayl nyn staartaghyn.”

Ren ny obbreeyn soiaghey dy jannoo stholk. Rish shiaghtin, cha row peiagh erbee gobbraghey. 'Sy stholk, hass ny obbreeyn ec giat y thie-obbree as ren ad çhionnraa. Va cowraghyn mooarey oc: “Nyn staartey, nyn mea!” Haink ny pabyryn-naight dy chlashtyn y çhionnraa, as va'n stholk er y çhellveeish.

Va turneyr ec ny obbreeyn: Honora Brackley. Ren y turneyr lhaih ny conaantyn oc. “Ta'n leigh lhiat,” dooyrt ee rish Clarence. “Cha nod ny stiureyderyn obbree y chur magh gyn three meeghyn dy hraa.”

Ec y jerrey, haink oaseir veih'n reiltys. Va'n oaseir shen cliaghtey ve ny obbree hene ayns thie-obbree. Ren ee ny obbreeyn as ny stiureyderyn y chur ry-cheilley ayns un shamyr.

“Ta feme ec ny greieyn noa er sleih,” dooyrt yn oaseir. “Ta feme oc er sleih dy stiurey ad, as dy hoiaghey ad kiart dagh shiaghtin. My vees ny greieyn kiart, bee ad gobbraghey rish ymmodee bleeantyn.”

Dooyrt ny stiureyderyn dy jinnagh ad cur traenal da ny obbreeyn son qualleeaght noa. Lesh y qualleeaght noa, foddee dagh obbree stiurey y greie as y greie y hoiaghey kiart. Bee ny obbreeyn er nyn eeck tra t'ad goll dys y traenal. Lurg y traenal, bee qualleeaght ec dagh fer jeu.

Hie ny obbreeyn erash gys yn obbyr. Va'n failley oc sauçhey, as dooyrt Clarence dy row'n eaghtyraneys feeu yn obbyr ooilley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va aggle er ny obbreeyn?
Son dy row ny stiureyderyn er ghra dy beagh kiare feed staartey caillit.
Cre ren ny obbreeyn 'sy stholk?
Hass ad ec giat y thie-obbree as ren ad çhionnraa.
Quoi va'n turneyr oc?
Honora Brackley va'n turneyr oc.
Cre ta ny greieyn noa feme?
T'ad feme sleih dy stiurey ad, as dy hoiaghey ad kiart.
Cre hooar ny obbreeyn?
Hooar ad traenal son qualleeaght noa, as va'n failley oc sauçhey.

lessons.title: Y çhellvane 'sy scoill
lessons.summary: At a school meeting in Peel, the head teacher Mortimer Glossop asks parents for their opinion on a restriction on phones: one father says middle-class children all have phones while poorer ones feel left out, the school's filter blocks pornography and secret groups, and Rosalie Pennock, who has doubts about a full ban, takes a promise from her son Lorimer to leave his phone downstairs at night.
lessons.text:
Ayns ard-scoill ayns Pheeil, va çhaglym son ny ayraghyn as ny moiraghyn. Va'n ard-ynseyder, Mortimer Glossop, laccal clashtyn tuarym ny ayraghyn as ny moiraghyn mychione çhellvaneyn.

“Ta mee smooinaghtyn mychione lhiettalys,” dooyrt Mortimer. “Lesh y lhiettalys shoh, cha bee çhellvane erbee ec scollag 'sy scoill, ec traa erbee 'sy laa. Ta mee laccal clashtyn yn tuarym eu roish my nee'm soiaghey.”

Va tuarymyn anchasley ec ny ayraghyn. Dooyrt dooinney ayns y lhiattee: “She meanvrastyl yn lught-thie aym. Ta paitçhyn y veanvrastyl ooilley lesh çhellvaneyn deyrey. Agh cha nel berçhys ec dagh lught-thie. Ta paitçhyn ayns lught-thie boght, as cha nel ad booiagh son nagh vel çhellvane noa oc. Cha nel berçhys cur aigney mie da paitçhey. Lesh y lhiettalys, bee dagh paitçhey cosoylagh 'sy scoill.”

Dooyrt ben elley: “Ta aggle orrym mychione ny buill folliaghtagh er yn eddyr-voggyl. Ta possanyn folliaghtagh ayn, raad nagh vel fys ec ny ayraghyn er cre ta ny paitçhyn screeu.”

“Ta shen feer,” dooyrt Mortimer. “Ta sleih olk er yn eddyr-voggyl, as ta pornograafaght ayn neesht. 'Sy scoill, ta claare ain ta lhiettal pornograafaght as ny buill folliaghtagh shen. Agh cha nel y claare shen ec y thie.”

Va Rosalie Pennock soie ec y chooyl. Va ourys urree mychione y lhiettalys. Ta mac eck, Lorimer, ayns y scoill, as t'eh goaill çhellvane marish dys y scoill son dy vel eh goll er y bus. “Ta ourys orrym,” dooyrt ee. “Ta feme ec ny paitçhyn er çhellvane er y raad dys y thie. Agh ta mee coardail nagh lhisagh çhellvane ve ayns y laue 'sy lessoon.”

Ec y jerrey, ren Mortimer soiaghey: bee lhiettalys er çhellvaneyn 'sy lessoon, agh cha nee 'sy laa slane.

'Sy thie, ren Rosalie loayrt rish Lorimer. “Ta mee laccal gialdynys voue,” dooyrt ee. “Bee'n çhellvane ayd heese 'sy thie ec yn oie, as cha jean oo jeeaghyn er tra t'ou ayns dty hamyr chadlee.”

Smooinee Lorimer rish tammylt. “Shen gialdynys,” dooyrt eh. Hug eh e laue da e voir. Ghow e voir yn gialdynys shen.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va Mortimer laccal clashtyn?
V'eh laccal clashtyn tuarym ny ayraghyn as ny moiraghyn.
Cre dooyrt y dooinney mychione berçhys?
Dooyrt eh nagh vel berçhys ec dagh lught-thie, as nagh vel berçhys cur aigney mie da paitçhey.
Cre ta'n claare 'sy scoill lhiettal?
T'eh lhiettal pornograafaght as ny buill folliaghtagh.
Row ourys er Rosalie?
Va. Va ourys urree mychione y lhiettalys.
Cre'n gialdynys hug Lorimer?
Hug eh gialdynys dy beagh y çhellvane echey heese ec yn oie.
